Pilot Sample Size for Sequential AIPE: Squared Multiple Correlation Coefficient

Source: R/seq_aipe_R2.R
seq_aipe_R2_pilot.Rd

Returns the number of observations to collect before the sequential accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) stopping rule for the population squared multiple correlation coefficient is evaluated for the first time with seq_aipe_R2.

Usage

seq_aipe_R2_pilot(
  width,
  p,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  ci_method = c("wald", "log_transformed"),
  m_0 = p + 2
)

Arguments

width

The target full width of the confidence interval for the population squared multiple correlation coefficient (\(\omega\) in the article). A single number greater than 0 and less than 1.

p

The number of predictors in the regression (\(k\) in the article). A whole number of at least 1.

conf_level

The confidence level (default 0.95). A single number strictly between 0 and 1.

ci_method

Which confidence interval the procedure is built on: "wald" (the default) or "log_transformed". See seq_aipe_R2.

m_0

The smallest pilot sample size allowed. A whole number of at least p + 2, which is also the default. (The other pilot sample size functions in this package default to 4; here the smallest usable sample depends on the number of predictors.)

Value

A length one integer: the pilot sample size.

Details

Kelley, Darku, and Chattopadhyay (2019, p. 505, and Appendix C, Equations 95 and 97) give a pilot sample size for each of the two confidence intervals they study. With \(p\) predictors (\(k\) in the article), target full width \(\omega\), and standard normal quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\):

  • ci_method = "wald": \(\max\{p, 4 z_{1-\alpha/2}/\omega\}\), rounded up to a whole number;

  • ci_method = "log_transformed": \(p + 2\).

The value returned is the larger of that size and m_0. The article prints \(4 z_{1-\alpha/2}/\omega\) without saying how it is made a whole number; rounding up is what reproduces the mean final sample sizes of its Tables 13 and 14 in the conditions where most replications stop at the pilot sample size.

With \(p + 1\) or fewer observations the sample squared multiple correlation is identically 1, so m_0 is at least \(p + 2\) and the returned pilot sample size is never smaller than that. This departs from the article's expression for the Wald interval only when \(\lceil 4 z_{1-\alpha/2}/\omega \rceil < p + 2\), that is, for a wide target with many predictors; it never happens in the conditions of the article's tables.

For the log transformed interval the article's pilot sample size of \(p + 2\) lets the procedure stop within a few observations of the pilot when the sample value happens to be near 0 or near 1, and the article's Tables 11 and 12 show the loss of coverage that follows. With either interval, a pilot sample that is not much larger than the number of predictors gives a sample value that is far too high, and the procedure can then stop at once with an interval that misses the population value. Raising m_0 guards against both. seq_aipe_R2 attaches a note to an interval reported from fewer than \(p \max(20, 2p)\) observations (20 per predictor, or \(2p\) per predictor with more than 10 predictors); an m_0 of that size keeps every check out of that range, at the price of a larger sample whenever the stopping rule would have been met earlier. In simulations with 5, 10, and 20 predictors, population values of .30 to .90, widths of .20 and .30, and a 95% level, coverage with the Wald interval was then between .896 and .932, where the default pilot sample size gave between .019 and .932. See the measured coverage in the help for seq_aipe_R2, and use seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity to check a planned design.

References

Kelley, K., Darku, F. B., & Chattopadhyay, B. (2019). Sequential accuracy in parameter estimation for population correlation coefficients. Psychological Methods, 24(4), 492–515. doi:10.1037/met0000203

Kelley, K. (2008). Sample size planning for the squared multiple correlation coefficient: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 43(4), 524–555. doi:10.1080/00273170802490632

See also

seq_aipe_R2, seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity; in DMAR, the fixed sample size planner ss_aipe_R2.

Other seq_aipe_R2: seq_aipe_R2(), seq_aipe_R2_sensitivity()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu, Francis Bilson Darku fbilsond@nd.edu, Bhargab Chattopadhyay bhargab@iiitvadodara.ac.in

Examples

# Three predictors of job satisfaction; a 95% confidence interval for the
# population squared multiple correlation no wider than 0.20.
seq_aipe_R2_pilot(width = 0.20, p = 3)
#> [1] 40

# The log transformed interval starts from p + 2 unless m_0 raises it.
seq_aipe_R2_pilot(width = 0.20, p = 3, ci_method = "log_transformed")
#> [1] 5
seq_aipe_R2_pilot(width = 0.20, p = 3, ci_method = "log_transformed",
                  m_0 = 30)
#> [1] 30
